B1: The screwdriver runs to a target torque (0.5 N m in the data); torque builds up only when the screw head seats, so without a screw it never builds up.
B2: An extra washer adds thickness under the head, so the screw seats after fewer turns and the torque rises earlier; the tightening otherwise completes normally.
B3: A damaged thread (filed screw, or filed/chipped hole) changes engagement and rundown friction, so seating can come earlier or later, and the screw can jam, raising the reaction torque at the wrist.
B4: Without a screw nothing engages the thread, so the axial force the robot feels while screwing is lower.
B5: Missing screws were mostly produced by skipping the pick-up (the robot waits 50 ms instead of loosening a screw), which shows in the loosening sample that precedes the tightening.
B6: A damaged screw travels with that screw while a damaged hole stays at its pin, so recurrence over cycles tells them apart. AURSAD records the pin but not the screw identity, so recurrence with a screw cannot be observed in the data.
